title: SOME/IP: Help debugging SOME/IP configuration
description:
SOME/IP payload dissector configuration can be quite challenging. This
patch adds optional debug output (default off) to simplify debugging
SOME/IP payload dissector configuration.

notes.body:
added 4 commits
  • 0313d274...57474232 - 3 commits from branch wireshark:master
  • 656f274f - SOME/IP: Help debugging SOME/IP configuration
[Compare with previous version](/wireshark/wireshark/-/merge_requests/18758/diffs?diff_id=1235712462&start_sha=0313d27416a31ad5fb5af1cc15531cbd2a117f44)
Doesn't this hide the text completly? ...text_internal is not supposed to be used in dissectors. Perhaps use the logging system instead?
+1 not big fan to use internal function

I understand but this is the only way I found to add text to the dissection tree. This is basically an annotation for the line before.

So logging does not work.

What would be a better way to do that?

changed this line in [version 3 of the diff](/wireshark/wireshark/-/merge_requests/18758/diffs?diff_id=1237409807&start_sha=656f274f61958f166c66ce528d0c89d59bfd30b4#939d770822ae6ea95241591ea801aa75281c2840_2772_2770)
Not perfect but I just add it to the fields.

The a bit cludgy replacement for ...add_text... is proto_tree_add_subtree_format() I think. The wholer idea being to discurage the use of add text instead of proto_tree_add_item() with a filter. This was heavily used in older code.  I thought the "add_hiden" would actually hide the text from the tree completely, used to create hidden filters like ip.address.

The amended code is fine though.
Hidden was, so that you have to set preferences -> protocols -> show hidden

I think the API is missing something like `proto_tree_add_subtree_format()` but without the subtree. The `proto_tree_add_text_internal()` does the correct thing, if you want to add an information to the tree but do not want to create a full header field with filters as this is not a field.

Problem was that it was missused and some dissectors used it for large part
of the dissection creating no filters for the protocol. But in general I
agree.

Den fre 17 jan. 2025 17:09Dr. Lars Völker (@LarsVoelker) <
gitlab@mg.gitlab.com> skrev:

It's generally discouraged to add something to the tree that isn't filterable. If it's not a field or generated field, a lot of time a FT_NONE is appropriate, which adds a text with no field value without a subtree. (In fact, there are reasons to prefer adding a FT_NONE and then a subtree to that item rather than `proto_tree_add_subtree_format()`.)

Most of the rest of the time a debug comment should be an expert info (perhaps with a low severity level).
A problem with not creating a field abbreviation is that it makes it difficult to have good JSON output - #17125

Understood and in general it makes perfect sense.

What I wanted to do here is allowing to see some configured IDs, if you wanted, so that you have an easier time to debug the complex payload dissection configuration. As the payload could get quite nested, a log output would not work IMHO.

The expert info is IMHO not a good solution here because it would add lot to the dissection tree and would be getting quite confusing.

And I guess it mightnot really make sense to even have this information in JSON as this is a very special case.

Anyhow, I can live with adding a bit text to some of the fields at the end for now as this is probably a very advanced use case that more than 95% of the users will never need to know about.
